cards.text: Picture it, baker. Israel hasn't crossed the Jordan River yet, and the land God promised is waiting on the other side. Moses, Israel's leader, stands up with the elders of Israel and tells the people, "Keep all the commandments I am giving you today."
Then he gets specific: on the very day they cross the Jordan, they set up large stones and coat them with plaster. Kind of like icing a sugar cookie so the letters show up.

cards.question: Moses wants those big stones coated with plaster so something can go on them. What?

answers.text: All the words of this law
The names of the twelve tribes
The story of the river crossing

cards.question: Once Israel crosses the Jordan, the plastered stones go up on Mount ___.

cards.text: And it's not just stones with writing. They're to build an altar there too, an altar of stones to the LORD their God.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to shape the stones for that altar with iron tools.

cards.text: Uncut stones only, and on that altar they offer burnt offerings to the LORD. So a cookie stamper would be USELESS on Mount Ebal, because shaping things is my WHOLE job, friend!

cards.question: When Israel sacrifices peace offerings on Mount Ebal, they eat them and ___ in the presence of the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses comes back to those stones: write all the words of this law, and write them distinctly, no blurry stamps. Trust me, baker, I stamped blurry for YEARS, and nobody wants a blurry law.
Now Moses and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel.

cards.question: What's the first thing Moses and the Levitical priests tell all Israel to do?
Moses and the priests tell Israel what they've become this day. What is it?
Because Israel is now the LORD's people, Moses and the priests say they shall obey His voice and follow His commandments.

cards.text: That same day, Moses gives the tribes their spots for after the crossing. Six tribes stand on Mount Gerizim: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.

cards.question: What are the six tribes on Mount Gerizim there to do?

cards.text: The other six stand on Mount Ebal: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali. Twelve tribes on two mountains, six and six, and somebody put REAL thought into this seating chart.

cards.question: The six tribes on Mount Ebal are there to bless the people too.

cards.text: Then the Levites get the loud part: they proclaim to every Israelite in a loud voice. Mags would've LOVED this job.
First up: cursed is the man who makes a carved idol or molten image and sets it up in secret.

cards.question: After the Levites call out the curse on the secret idol, what are all the people to say?

cards.text: And the people are to say it after every single curse, twelve curses and twelve Amens. A whole nation told to agree out loud, and I can't get my ovens to agree on ONE temperature.

cards.question: The next curse falls on whoever dishonors his father or mother.
The next curse: cursed is he who moves his neighbor's ___ stone.
One curse is about a blind man. What does the cursed person do to him?

answers.text: Lets him wander in the road
Turns him away at the gate

cards.question: Next, cursed is he who withholds ___ from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow.

cards.text: Then come four curses about forbidden relations: no sleeping with your father's wife, your sister or your mother-in-law, and no lying with any animal.

cards.question: Then a curse on the man who strikes down his neighbor in ___.
The next curse is on someone who kills an innocent person. What's behind it?
The last curse is only on the priests who don't put the words of this law into practice.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave the two mountains for now. Moses isn't done preaching, friend, not even close.

findings.problem: Most choice cards in stop 2 depend on luck. Cards 9, 10, 11, 12 and 15 each ask about a curse the baker hasn't heard yet. No story card sets up any of them: card 8 covers only the Amen pattern. Cards 2 and 7 are discovery questions too. Discovery picks make up most of the stop, not just a few.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. ... A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording of a curse they have never seen ("moves his neighbor's ___ stone"). Nothing told so far lets them reason out "boundary" over "altar" or "grinding."

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish the wording of an unseen curse ("withholds ___ from the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow"). No story card leads them to "justice" over "land" or "shelter," and withholding shelter from a widow is also something a baker could argue is the answer.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to guess a detail of an unseen curse: what is done to the blind man. It has no setup, so it works like the bad Psalm 23 example ("What does He anoint David's head with?"). It doesn't ask about movement or meaning. For example, it could ask what several curses have in common, such as people who can't protect themselves.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to guess an unseen detail: what is behind the killing of an innocent person (a bribe). Nothing told earlier points to "He accepts a bribe" over "He loses his temper" or "He settles an old score," so only luck gets it right.

rule.text: If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line nearly copies the doc's example. "And that's where we'll leave the two mountains for now" closely matches "And that's where we'll leave it for now."

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: Card 17 holds only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse. It still cites Deuteronomy 27:26, which card 16 already asked about.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?

findings.problem: This story card is bare narration with none of Papa Dorin's voice: "Now Moses and the Levitical priests speak to all Israel." It is there only to set up card 11.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
